title: The king of the ghazal: Pir Fazal Gujrati
titleOriginal: غزل دا بادشاہ پیر سید فضل شاہ گجراتی رحمۃ اللہ علیہ
takeaway: A true master teaches by who he is, not only by what he writes.
scene: An elegy for Pir Syed Fazal Shah Gujrati, a famous Sufi poet called 'the king of the ghazal'. Dr. Ahmad clearly saw him as his own teacher and guide.

original: ڈگیا میرے سر دا سائیں رس گئیاں تقدیراں
چادر صبر قرار میرے دی ہو گئی لیراں لیراں
transliteration: Diggya mere sir da saaeen, russ gaiyaan taqdeeraan
Chaadar sabr qaraar mere di ho gayi leeraan leeraan
translation: The protector over my head has fallen; fate has turned against me.
The shawl of my patience and peace has been torn to shreds.
couplets.story: His master and protector has died. It feels like fate itself has turned against him, and his calm has been ripped to pieces like an old shawl.

original: فضل ملنگ جیہے لعل انملے کدی کدائیں ملدے
موت ملاندی مٹی دے وچ چن جیہیاں تصویراں
transliteration: Fazal malang jihe laal anmulle kadi kadaaeen milde
Maut milaandi mitti de vich chann jihiyaan tasveeraan
translation: Priceless rubies like Fazal, that carefree man of God, are found only once in a while;
death mixes faces as lovely as the moon into the dust.
couplets.story: People like Fazal are as rare as priceless jewels. You meet one only once in a long while. Death takes even the most beautiful people and returns them to the earth.

original: سوہنی دے گجرات توں اٹھیا سوہنا شکھر سیانا
سخن وری دا دیوا بلیا پھیل گئیاں تنویراں
transliteration: Sohni de Gujraat ton uthiya sohna shikhar siyaana
Sukhan-vari da deeva baliya, phail gaiyaan tanveeraan
translation: From Sohni's own Gujrat rose a beautiful, wise and towering man;
the lamp of poetry was lit, and its light spread everywhere.
couplets.story: He came from Gujrat, the same town as Sohni in the old love story. From there, a wise and brilliant man rose up and lit the lamp of poetry, and its light spread everywhere.

original: چہرہ چانن بول رسیلے فکروں رومی جامی
علم ادب دے کول خزانے دل سی وانگ فقیراں
transliteration: Chehra chaanan, bol raseele, fikron Rumi Jami
Ilm adab de kol khazaane, dil si vaang faqeeraan
translation: A face full of light, sweet words, in thought a Rumi or a Jami;
he held treasures of learning and literature, yet his heart was like a humble faqir's.
couplets.story: His face shone, his words were sweet, and his thinking was as deep as the great Persian Sufi poets Rumi and Jami. He knew a huge amount, but his heart stayed humble, like a poor holy man's.

original: ذکر فکر تے علم حلم وچ اوسی فقر یگانہ
حد تکبر والیاں آئیاں نیڑے نہ تقصیراں
transliteration: Zikr fikr te ilm hilm vich osi faqr yagaana
Hadd takabbur vaaliyaan aaiyaan nere na taqseeraan
translation: In remembrance of God, reflection, knowledge and gentleness, his poverty of spirit was unmatched;
the faults of pride never came anywhere near him.
couplets.story: He spent his time remembering God and thinking deeply. He was learned and gentle, and he never let pride touch him.

original: شعراں بولاں وچ حلاوت پختہ علموں عقلوں
ایہہ صفتاں نیں میرے ویروں شاعر دیاں جاگیراں
transliteration: Shairaan bolaan vich halaavat, pukhta ilmon aqlon
Eh siftaan nain mere veero, shaair diyaan jaageeraan
translation: Sweetness in his verses and his speech, mature in knowledge and wisdom:
my brothers, these qualities are a poet's true estates.
couplets.story: His poems and his words were sweet, and he was wise and well educated. The poet says these are a poet's real riches, worth more than land or property.

original: بحر ادب دے تارو جگ وچ ہے سن گرو ہزاراں
پیر میرے دی سخن وری دیاں کتے نہ ملن نظیراں
transliteration: Behr-e-adab de taaroo jag vich hai san guru hazaaraan
Pir mere di sukhan-vari diyaan kitte na milan nazeeraan
translation: There have been thousands of teachers swimming in the ocean of literature,
but nowhere can you find anything to match my master's poetry.
couplets.story: There have been thousands of good poets and teachers. Nobody's poetry comes close to his master's.

original: سوز فراق تے عشق دے روگی نویں حیاتی پاندے
پیر فضل دے شعراں اندر بھریاں ہین تاثیراں
transliteration: Soz-e-firaaq te ishq de rogi naveen hayaati paande
Pir Fazal de shairaan andar bhariyaan hain taaseeraan
translation: People burning with separation and sick with love find new life:
Pir Fazal's verses are full of healing power.
couplets.story: People who are heartbroken or lovesick read Pir Fazal's poems and feel alive again. His words have a real healing power.

original: شعر سخن دے امبر اتے تا قیامت رہسی
پیر فضل داناواں روشن وانگوں شاہ کبیراں
transliteration: Shair sukhan de ambar utte taa qiyaamat rehsi
Pir Fazal da naavaan roshan vaangon Shah Kabeeraan
translation: In the sky of poetry, until Judgment Day,
Pir Fazal's name will shine like the great kings.
couplets.story: In the sky of poetry, Pir Fazal's name will keep shining until the end of time, like the names of great kings.

original: خادم سید شاہ ولہ دا حسبوں نسبوں اعلیٰ
فیض اوہدے دیاں دل میرے تے وکھو وکھ لکیراں
transliteration: Khaadim Syed Shah Daulah da, hasbon nasbon aala
Faiz ohde diyaan dil mere te vakho vakh lakeeraan
translation: A servant of Syed Shah Daulah, noble in family and lineage;
his blessings have left their own distinct lines on my heart.
couplets.story: He came from a noble family and served the shrine of the saint Shah Daulah. His kindness and blessings have left their marks on the poet's heart.

original: شعر کلام دی دنیا اندر احمدؔ کون نمانا
پیر فضل داناواں روشن وانگوں بدر منیراں
transliteration: Shair kalaam di duniya andar Ahmad kaun nimaana
Pir Fazal da naavaan roshan vaangon badr-e-muneeraan
translation: In the world of poetry, who is humble Ahmad?
Pir Fazal's name shines like the radiant full moon.
couplets.story: He ends humbly. Who is he, Ahmad, in the world of poetry? It's his master's name that shines like the full moon.

deeper: This poem is a disciple's tribute to his pir, his spiritual and poetic master. It paints the ideal Sufi: deep learning held with a 'heart like a faqir', remembrance, reflection, and no pride. That is the kind of person this whole book hopes to become. Comparing him to Rumi and Jami places him in the great line of mystic poets.
why: It helps readers see where Dr. Ahmad learned his craft, and what he admired most in a person.
prompt: Who is a teacher or mentor whose example has shaped you? What did you learn from who they were?
notes: Couplet 10: 'Shah Daulah' is read as the famous saint of Gujrat, Shah Daulah Daryai; the printed text is 'شاہ ولہ'.
